standards.name: PSI Extended FASTA Format (PEFF)
standards.abstract: PEFF defines a plain-text extension of the FASTA flat-file format for protein and nucleotide sequence databases used in proteomics. It represents sequence database metadata (database name, version, source, number of entries, sequence type) in a header block and extends individual FASTA entry definition lines with structured keys for identifiers, taxonomy, processed sequences, variants, modifications (including ontology references like PSI-MOD/UNIMOD), and other annotations. The specification is maintained by the HUPO Proteomics Standards Initiative (PSI) and aims to enable consistent extraction and interpretation of sequence, taxonomy and structural annotations (PTMs, variants, processed regions, proteoforms) by search engines, spectral library tools, alignment software and repositories. The project provides a main specification document, controlled-vocabulary integration, example files, validators and reference implementations (e.g. Proteomics::PEFF, online PEFF validator) and has been ratified through the PSI document process.

classification.rationale: The source material includes explicit field-level tables (CV-DatabaseFormat spreadsheet and specification sections listing header and entry keys with concrete formats and examples). These name individual metadata keys and give concrete data formats (integer, URL, CV term, specific structured string patterns), so the standard is best represented as a Metadata Table.

standards.notes: Fields extracted from the CV-DatabaseFormat spreadsheet and PEFF specification drafts. For structured string fields (Processed, Variant, ModRes, VariantSimple etc.) the specification defines internal formats (position|value|term) — these are represented here as string types with the exact format documented in raw_full_info and evidence quotes. The PEFF specification also integrates CV/ontology references (PSI-MOD, UNIMOD) and recommends controlled vocabularies for many keys.
